definition: Calcitonin is a 32-amino-acid polypeptide hormone whose receptors are found in several body tissues, including the brain. In psychology-related contexts, it may be mentioned because it has been studied as an add-on pain treatment and may affect pain through serotonin-related activity and reduced abnormal nerve firing.
